# Abstract {.unnumbered}

This report presents a comprehensive analysis of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Question Answering system built on the HotpotQA dataset. The system implements a sophisticated multi-stage pipeline, including modular data ingestion, chunking, dense and sparse embedding, hybrid retrieval, late-interaction re-ranking, smart query routing, and LLM-powered generation with chain-of-thought prompting.

Key innovations include the adoption of BAAI's BGE-M3 for unified dense-sparse retrieval, on-the-fly ColBERT re-ranking to resolve multi-hop information dependencies, a pre-retrieval smart router for intent classification, and a MongoDB-backed conversational persistence layer.

Automated evaluations on a synthetic HotpotQA subset demonstrate that the hybrid retriever achieves a Hit Rate@3 of 1.000 and a Recall@5 of 0.940, indicating high search robustness. The LLM generator, evaluated using Gemini-3.1-flash-lite as a judge, achieves an overall RAGAS evaluation score of 0.9437, demonstrating high faithfulness (1.000) and answer correctness (0.9671) after filtering. The resulting system balances high accuracy with low conversational latency, serving as a robust foundation for multi-hop QA tasks.
